Lily and Max liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like hats and books and toys. One day, they saw a big box with a picture of a monkey on it. They opened the box and found a brown monkey with a long tail. It was soft and cute.

"Look, Max, a monkey!" Lily said. "Can we keep it?"

Max nodded. He liked the monkey too. He took it out of the box and hugged it. The monkey had a button on its chest. Max pressed the button and the monkey made a funny sound. It said, "Ooh-ooh-ah-ah!"

Lily and Max laughed. They played with the monkey and made it say, "Ooh-ooh-ah-ah!" They put a hat on its head and a scarf around its neck. They pretended it was their pet.

They found a hook on the wall and decided to hang the monkey there. They thought it would be fun to see it swing from its tail. They lifted the monkey and put its tail on the hook. The monkey looked happy.

"Bye-bye, monkey!" Lily said. "We will come back and play with you again!"

They closed the box and went down the stairs. They did not know that the monkey had a secret. When they were gone, the monkey pressed its own button and said, "Ooh-ooh-ah-ah! I'm free!" It jumped off the hook and ran around the attic. It was not a toy. It was a real monkey. And it was very naughty.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play outside in the sun. One day, they see a big hill with many trees. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side.

They hold hands and start to walk up the hill. They see many birds and flowers and bugs. They are happy and curious. They talk to each other and laugh.

"Look, Tom, a red bird!" Mia says, pointing to the sky.

"Wow, it is so pretty!" Tom says, looking up.

But as they look up, they do not see where they are going. They stumble on a rock and fall down. They hurt their knees and elbows. They cry and hug each other.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Mia says, rubbing her knee.

"Are you okay, Mia?" Tom says, wiping his tears.

"I think so, Tom. Are you okay?" Mia says, looking at his elbow.

"I think so, too. But look, what is that?" Tom says, pointing to something black and gray on the ground.

They see a pile of ash. It is from a fire that burned some of the trees. It is still warm and smoky. They are scared and curious.

"What is it, Tom?" Mia says, touching the ash.

"It is ash, Mia. It is what is left after something burns. It is not good to touch. It can hurt you." Tom says, pulling her hand away.

"Who burned the trees, Tom?" Mia says, looking around.

"I don't know, Mia. Maybe someone who is lazy and does not care about the trees. Or maybe it was an accident. But we should not stay here. It is not safe. Let's go back." Tom says, holding her hand.

"Okay, Tom. Let's go back. Maybe we can find another hill to climb. One that is green and happy." Mia says, nodding.

They get up and walk back down the hill. They are careful and watch where they are going. They see the red bird again and wave to it. They are happy and curious. They talk to each other and laugh.

Tim and Kim are twins who like to play in the park. They have a big red ball that they kick and throw to each other. One day, they see a new slide in the park. It is shiny and tall and has a spiral shape. Tim and Kim want to try the slide, but there is a long line of kids waiting for their turn.

"Can we go on the slide, please?" Tim asks their mom.

"Sure, but you have to wait your turn and be polite," their mom says.

Tim and Kim nod and join the line. But they are very impatient. They want to go on the slide now. They start to whine and fidget and push the other kids.

"Stop that, Tim and Kim," their mom says. "You have to be patient and wait your turn. If you don't, we will go home."

Tim and Kim stop whining and pushing, but they are still unhappy. They look at the slide and wish they could go on it.

Suddenly, they hear a loud noise. They see their big red ball rolling down the hill. It is going fast and heading towards the road. There are cars and trucks on the road. Tim and Kim are scared. They don't want their ball to get hit by a car or a truck.

"Mom, our ball!" they shout.

Their mom sees the ball and runs after it. She tries to catch it, but it is too fast. She sees a gap in the traffic and runs across the road. She grabs the ball and saves it. She is happy and relieved. She brings the ball back to Tim and Kim.

"Mom, you saved our ball!" they say. "Thank you, thank you!"

They hug their mom and kiss her. They are happy and grateful. They don't care about the slide anymore. They just want to play with their ball and their mom.

They go to a grassy spot and play with their ball. They kick and throw it to each other and to their mom. They laugh and have fun. They are not impatient anymore. They are glad that their mom saved their ball and their land.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. Today they go to the park with their moms. They see a trail in the park. The trail has many leaves and rocks.

"Let's go on the trail!" Anna says.

"OK!" Ben says.

They run on the trail. They see a big puddle. The puddle is wet and shiny.

"Look, a puddle!" Ben says.

"Can we jump in it?" Anna asks.

"Yes, but be careful!" their moms say.

Anna and Ben jump in the puddle. They splash and laugh. The water is cold and fun. They get wet and muddy.

"That was fun!" Anna says.

"Yes, it was!" Ben says.

They hug and smile. Their moms give them towels and hugs. They go home happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They share a room and a bed. They like to play and talk before they sleep. But sometimes they fight over toys and books.

One night, Anna wanted to read a book about a judge. A judge is a person who decides who is right and who is wrong. Ben wanted to play with a small car. A small car is a toy that can move and make noises.

"Give me the book, Anna. I want to read it too," Ben said.

"No, Ben. It is my book. You can play with your car," Anna said.

They pulled and pushed the book. They shouted and cried. They woke up their mom and dad.

Mom and dad came to their room. They were not happy. They looked at Anna and Ben.

"What is going on here? Why are you fighting? It is time to sleep," mom said.

"Anna took my book. She is not fair," Ben said.

"Ben took my car. He is not nice," Anna said.

Mom and dad sighed. They took the book and the car. They put them on a shelf.

"Listen, Anna and Ben. You are twins. You are family. You should share and care for each other. Fighting is not good. It makes you and others unhappy. Do you understand?" dad said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They felt sorry. They hugged each other.

"I am sorry, Anna. You can read the book tomorrow. I love you," Ben said.

"I am sorry, Ben. You can play with the car tomorrow. I love you," Anna said.

Mom and dad smiled. They kissed Anna and Ben. They tucked them in.

"Good night, Anna and Ben. Sleep well. We love you," mom and dad said.

Anna and Ben closed their eyes. They felt warm and cozy. They dreamed of judges and cars. They were happy.

Ben and Jen are twins. They like to play on the farm with their grandpa. Grandpa has many animals, but his favorite is Molly the mule. Molly is brown and big and strong. She helps grandpa carry things and plow the field.

One day, Ben and Jen want to ride Molly. They ask grandpa, and he says yes, but they have to be careful and gentle. He gives them a hat and a scarf to wear, because it is cold outside. He also gives them a carrot to give to Molly as a treat.

Ben and Jen go to the barn, where Molly is waiting. They say hello to Molly and pet her soft fur. They give her the carrot, and she eats it with a loud crunch. Then they climb on her back, one in front of the other. Grandpa helps them with a rope to hold on to.

Molly starts to walk slowly around the farm. Ben and Jen are happy and excited. They see the cows, the sheep, the chickens, and the ducks. They wave to them and say their names. Molly makes a funny noise with her mouth, like she is talking to them too.

But then, Molly sees something that makes her angry. It is a red cloth that someone has hung on a fence. Molly does not like red. She thinks it is scary and bad. She stops walking and starts to kick and buck. She tries to get Ben and Jen off her back. She runs towards the cloth and tries to rip it with her teeth.

Ben and Jen are scared and sad. They hold on to the rope and to each other. They cry for grandpa to help them. Grandpa hears them and runs to them. He grabs the rope and pulls Molly away from the cloth. He calms her down and talks to her softly. He takes Ben and Jen off her back and hugs them. He says they are brave and good. He says Molly is naughty and sorry.

Ben and Jen forgive Molly, but they do not want to ride her again. They say goodbye to her and give her a pat. They go back to the house with grandpa. He gives them some hot cocoa and cookies. He tells them a story about when he was a boy and rode a mule. He says mules are smart and loyal, but sometimes they are stubborn and silly. He says he loves Molly, even when she is naughty. Ben and Jen love grandpa, and they love Molly too. They smile and sip their cocoa. They are happy and warm.

Lily and Ben went to the shop with Mom. They wanted to buy a treat for being good. Mom said they could choose one thing each.

Lily saw a plastic doll with long hair and a pink dress. She liked the doll very much. She said, "Mom, can I buy this doll? She is so pretty and I can comb her hair."

Ben saw a plastic car with big wheels and a loud horn. He liked the car very much. He said, "Mom, can I buy this car? It is so fast and I can make it beep."

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can buy the doll and the car. They are not very expensive and you have been good. But first, let's buy some fruit for later. Fruit is delicious and healthy."

Lily and Ben agreed and helped Mom pick some apples, bananas and grapes. They put them in a bag and paid at the counter. Then they took their plastic toys and went home.

They were very happy with their new toys. They played with them all afternoon. They also ate some fruit and shared with Mom. They said, "Thank you, Mom, for buying us these toys and fruit. They are both delicious." Mom hugged them and said, "You're welcome, my sweeties. I love you very much."

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with red apples on it. They wanted to pick some apples to eat, but the tree was too high for them.

"Look, there is a ladder!" Ben said. He pointed to a wooden ladder that was hidden behind some bushes. "We can use it to climb the tree and get the apples."

Lily was not sure. She thought the ladder looked old and shaky. She was afraid it might break or fall. "I don't think we should use that ladder," she said. "It is not safe. Maybe the apples belong to someone else."

Ben did not listen to Lily. He ran to the ladder and started to climb. He reached the first branch and grabbed an apple. He smiled and said, "This apple is so juicy and sweet. Come on, Lily, don't be scared. There are more apples for us."

Lily shook her head. She stayed on the ground and watched Ben. She hoped he would be careful. But then, she heard a loud crack. The ladder broke and Ben fell down. He hit the ground hard and cried out in pain.

Lily ran to Ben and saw that he had hurt his arm and leg. She felt sorry for him and tried to help him. She said, "Ben, are you okay? I'm sorry you fell. We should go and find a grown-up to help you."

Ben nodded and said, "Lily, you were right. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. The ladder was not safe. The apples were not worth it. I'm sorry I was greedy and foolish."

Lily and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned that they should be careful and respectful. They learned that they should listen to their friends and not take what is not theirs. They learned that sometimes, the best things are not hidden, but right in front of them.

Sam and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were lions and tigers. They would run and jump and roar at each other. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they found a big jug in the shed. It was empty and had a handle and a spout. Sam had an idea. He said to Mia, "Let's fill the jug with water and use it as a fountain. We can be lions and tigers who drink from the fountain."

Mia liked the idea. They took the jug to the tap and filled it with water. Then they carried it to the middle of the garden and put it on the ground. They took turns to tilt the jug and make the water come out of the spout. They pretended to lap up the water with their tongues and make happy noises.

They were having so much fun that they did not hear their mum calling them for lunch. She came out to the garden and saw them playing with the jug. She smiled and said, "You two look like very thirsty lions and tigers. Do you want to come inside and have some sandwiches and juice?"

Sam and Mia nodded and ran to their mum. They gave her a hug and said, "Thank you, mum. We love you." They left the jug in the garden. It was peaceful and quiet. The sun shone on the water and made it sparkle. The jug was happy too. It had made two new friends.

Jill liked to play with snow. She made snowballs and snowmen with her friends. She wore a pink hat and a pink coat and pink gloves. She was very popular and everyone wanted to be her friend.

One day, a new girl came to the park. Her name was Kate. She had a blue hat and a blue coat and no gloves. She looked cold and sad. Jill felt sorry for her and wanted to help her.

"Hi, I am Jill. Do you want to play with me?" Jill asked.

"Hi, I am Kate. I want to play, but I have no gloves. My hands are very cold," Kate said.

"That's okay. You can lend my gloves. They are very warm and pretty," Jill said. She took off her gloves and gave them to Kate.

"Thank you, Jill. You are very nice," Kate said. She put on the gloves and smiled.

Jill and Kate played with snow. They made snowballs and snowmen and had fun. Jill was happy to share her gloves with Kate.

But then, something bad happened. Kate saw some other kids playing with a sled. She wanted to try it too. She ran to the sled and jumped on it. She did not ask Jill or the other kids. She did not say goodbye. She just took the sled and the gloves and slid down the hill.

"Hey, that's not fair! That's our sled! And those are my gloves!" Jill shouted.

But Kate did not hear her. She did not care. She just kept sliding and laughing. She did not give back the sled or the gloves. She was very mean and selfish.

Jill was very sad and angry. She had no gloves and no sled and no friend. She felt cold and lonely. She cried and went home. She wished she never met Kate. She wished she never lent her gloves. She learned a hard lesson. Not everyone is nice and honest. Some people are bad and greedy. She had to be careful who she trusted.

Lily and Ben are twins. They share a room and a bed. They like to play and read and sing together. But sometimes they fight over toys and books and space.

One night, Lily and Ben are getting ready for bed. They brush their teeth and put on their pajamas. Then they climb into their bed and pick a book to read. Lily wants to read about princesses and dragons. Ben wants to read about cars and planes. They both pull the book they want and tug and tug.

"Let go of my book!" Lily says. "I want to read it first!"

"No, let go of my book!" Ben says. "I want to read it first!"

"Let's test our spears," Lila whispered to Rani. "You go left and I go right. We will throw our spears at the same time."

Rani nodded and they crept closer to the rabbit. They counted to three and threw their spears. But the rabbit was clever and saw them. It jumped away and ran into the bush.

"Oh no, we missed!" Lila said. "The rabbit is too fast and smart."

"Maybe we can trick it," Rani said. "Look, there is a carrot on the ground. We can use it as bait."

Rani picked up the carrot and placed it near the bush. She hid behind a tree and waited. Lila hid behind another tree and held her spear. They hoped the rabbit would come out and eat the carrot.

Soon, they heard a rustle in the bush. The rabbit poked its head out and sniffed the air. It saw the carrot and licked its lips. It hopped out of the bush and moved towards the carrot.

"Now!" Rani shouted. She and Lila threw their spears again. This time, they hit the rabbit and it fell to the ground.

"Yay, we got it!" Lila cheered. "We are good hunters!"

They ran to the rabbit and picked it up. They were proud of their spears and their clever plan. They took the rabbit home and cooked it for their dinner. The white dog does not like Lily. It barks and snaps at her. Lily is scared and sad. She runs back to Mom and Max. Mom hugs her and says, "Are you okay, Lily? That was a mean dog. It does not know how to be nice."

Max is angry at the white dog. He growls and shows his teeth. He wants to protect Lily. He does not like mean dogs. He thinks they are ignorant. He does not know what ignorant means, but he heard Mom say it once.

Mom sees Max growl. She says, "No, Max. Do not fight. We do not want trouble. Come, let's go to another part of the park. There are nicer dogs there." She pulls Max by his leash. Max nods and follows Mom. He trusts her. He looks at Lily and licks her face. He says, "I love you, Lily. You are a good girl." Lily smiles and says, "I love you too, Max. You are a good dog."

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight. One day, they want to play with the same toy car. Anna grabs the car first, but Ben pulls it hard. They both yell and tug at the car.

"Mine!" Anna says.

"No, mine!" Ben says.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees them fighting over the toy car. She is not happy. She takes the car away and puts it on a high shelf.

"Stop fighting, Anna and Ben. You need to share and take turns. Now, go to the bathroom and wash your hands. It is time for lunch," Mom says.

Anna and Ben are sad and angry. They do not want to go to the bathroom. They want the toy car. They walk slowly to the bathroom, still frowning. They see a big mirror on the wall. They look at themselves and make funny faces. They start to giggle and forget about the car.

They wash their hands and dry them with a towel. They see a bottle of soap on the sink. They open it and squeeze some soap on their hands. They rub their hands together and make bubbles. They blow the bubbles and watch them fly. They laugh and clap their hands.

They have fun with the soap and the bubbles. They do not hear Mom calling them for lunch. They do not see the soap and the water making a mess on the floor. They think the bathroom is perfect. They do not know that Mom will scream when she sees the bathroom.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they wake up very early. They want to see the sunrise.

They put on their coats and hats. They go to the hill near their house. They sit on the grass and wait. The sky is dark and quiet.

"Look, Lily, the sun is coming!" Tom says. He points to the horizon. He sees a bright orange ball. It is getting bigger and bigger.

"Wow, it is so pretty!" Lily says. She smiles and claps her hands. She sees the sky changing colors. It is pink and purple and yellow.

They watch the sunrise for a long time. They feel happy and warm. They talk and laugh and sing.

But then, Lily sees something. She sees a big rock behind Tom. It is rolling down the hill. It is coming fast.

"Tom, watch out!" Lily shouts. She tries to pull Tom away. But it is too late. The rock hits Tom. He falls down. He cries out loud.

Lily is scared. She runs to Tom. She hugs him and says sorry. She sees a cut on his knee. It is bleeding.

"Are you okay, Tom?" Lily asks. She feels sad and sorry.

Tom is hurt. He feels pain and angry. He pushes Lily away. He says, "Go away, Lily! You are not my friend! You made me fall!"

Lily is shocked. She does not understand. She did not make Tom fall. She tried to help him. She says, "No, Tom, I am your friend! I did not make you fall! The rock made you fall!"

But Tom does not listen. He gets up and limps away. He leaves Lily alone on the hill. He goes back to his house.

Lily is alone. She feels sad and lonely. She does not know what to do. She looks at the sunrise. It is not pretty anymore. It is just regular. She cries.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to bake. They baked cakes, pies, cookies and bread. They shared their treats with their families and neighbors. Everyone in town loved their baking.

One day, it was very cold and icy outside. Lily and Tom could not go out to play. They decided to bake something warm and yummy. They asked their moms for some flour, sugar, eggs, butter and milk. They also found some chocolate chips and nuts in the pantry.

They mixed everything in a big bowl and poured it into a pan. They put the pan in the oven and waited for it to bake. They smelled the sweet and nutty aroma of their cake. They were very excited to taste it.

When the cake was done, they took it out of the oven and let it cool. They cut two big slices and put some whipped cream on top. They sat down at the table and ate their cake. It was soft, moist and delicious.

They said to each other, "This is the best cake ever! We are very good bakers!"

They smiled and hugged. They were happy and warm, even though it was icy outside.

One day, Tom and Lily went to play in the snow. They put on their warm coats, hats, gloves and boots. They ran outside and saw the white powder on the ground. It was cold and soft.

"Let's make a snowman!" said Tom. He rolled a big ball of snow and put it on the grass. Then he rolled a smaller ball and put it on top of the big one. He found two sticks for the arms, a carrot for the nose, and some stones for the eyes and mouth.

"Look, our snowman is done!" said Lily. She wrapped a scarf around his neck and gave him a hat. "He looks happy!"

They heard a loud noise. It was a snow plow. It was big and gray and had a metal blade. It was clearing the road of snow.

"Watch out!" shouted Tom. He grabbed Lily's hand and pulled her away from the snowman. The snow plow came closer and closer. It pushed the snow to the side of the road.

"Stop!" cried Lily. "You're going to hit our snowman!"

But the snow plow did not stop. It hit the snowman and broke him into pieces. The snow flew in the air and landed on Tom and Lily. They were covered in snow.

They were very sad. They looked at the snow plow. The driver saw them and waved. He said he was sorry. He did not see their snowman.

"It's okay," said Tom. He hugged Lily. "We can make another snowman. But we have to put him somewhere safe."

They brushed off the snow from their clothes and went to find a new spot for their snowman. They decided to put him in their backyard, where the snow plow could not reach him. They smiled and started to roll new balls of snow. They were happy again.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. But they do not like to share. They always fight over who gets what.

One day, they find a yellow box in their closet. They do not know what is inside. They both want to open it. They pull and tug and yell.

"Give me the box! It is mine!" Anna says.

"No, it is mine! I saw it first!" Ben says.

They do not listen to each other. They do not care about each other's feelings. They only want the box.

Suddenly, the box breaks. It falls to the floor. Out comes a big mess. There are papers and crayons and stickers and glue. They are all over the room. They are all over Anna and Ben.

Anna and Ben stop fighting. They look at the mess. They feel sad and sorry. They wish they had not been so greedy and mean.

They look at each other. They say sorry.

"I am sorry, Anna. I should have shared with you. You are my sister. I love you." Ben says.

"I am sorry, Ben. I should have listened to you. You are my brother. I love you." Anna says.

They hug and smile. They decide to clean up the mess together. They use the papers and crayons and stickers and glue to make cards and pictures. They have fun and laugh. They share and care.

They learn a lesson. They learn that sharing is better than fighting. They learn that listening is better than yelling. They learn that love is better than greed.

They are happy. They are twins. They are friends.

Sara was lonely. She had no friends to play with. She liked to read stories, but she had read all her books. She wished she had a new story to read.

One day, she found a big book in the attic. It had many pictures and words. Sara opened the book and saw a story about a princess and a dragon. She wanted to read it, but the words were too hard. She could not read them.

She looked at the pictures and tried to guess what the story was. She saw the princess in a castle, the dragon in a cave, and a knight on a horse. She made up her own story in her head. She said, "The princess was sad. She wanted to go out and see the world. But the dragon was scary. He breathed fire and roared. He did not let anyone near the castle. The knight was brave. He wanted to save the princess. He rode his horse to the cave. He fought the dragon with his sword."

Sara turned the page and saw a picture of the princess and the knight hugging. She smiled and said, "The knight won. He beat the dragon. He freed the princess. They were happy. They kissed and hugged. They went away together."

She turned the page again and saw a picture of the dragon. He was not dead. He was crying. He had a bandage on his nose. He looked sad and lonely. Sara felt sorry for him. She said, "The dragon was not bad. He was lonely. He had no friends. He only wanted to play. He did not know how to be nice. He did not know how to share. He did not know how to love."

Sara closed the book and thought for a while. She had an idea. She said, "I will be the dragon's friend. I will teach him how to be nice. I will teach him how to share. I will teach him how to love. I will read him stories. He will not be lonely anymore. He will be happy."

She took the book and ran down the stairs. She went outside and looked for the dragon. She did not see him, but she heard him. He was in the woods, behind the house. He was still crying. Sara called out, "Hello, dragon! I have a story for you. Do you want to hear it?"

The dragon heard her voice and stopped crying. He was curious. He peeked out from the trees and saw a little girl with a big book. He said, "Who are you? What do you want?"

Sara smiled and said, "I am Sara. I want to be your friend. I have a story for you. It is about a princess and a knight and a dragon. Do you want to hear it?"

The dragon nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I like stories. But I have no one to read them to me."

Sara said, "I will read it to you. Come closer. Don't be afraid. I will not hurt you."

The dragon came closer and sat down next to Sara. He looked at the book and said, "What is this?"

Sara said, "This is a book. It has pictures and words. The words tell the story. The pictures show the story. I will read the words to you. You can look at the pictures. You can ask me questions. You can tell me what you think. You can taste the story with me."

The dragon said, "Taste the story? What does that mean?"

Sara said, "It means to enjoy the story. To feel the story. To imagine the story. To learn from the story. To love the story. Stories are yummy. They make us happy. They make us smart. They make us kind. They make us friends."

The dragon said, "I want to taste the story. I want to be happy. I want to be smart. I want to be kind. I want to be your friend."

Sara said, "Then let's taste the story together. Let's start from the beginning. Once upon a time, there was a princess and a dragon..."

Lily and Tom were very sad. They liked the slide. They wanted to play on it. They were also scared of the truck. They ran away from the park and looked for their mom. They found her at home. She was making cookies for them.

She said they could have some cookies and play with their toys. She said maybe the fog would go away soon and they could go back to the park.

Lily and Tom felt better. They ate some cookies and played with their toys. They hoped the slide would be fixed soon. They still liked the fog, but they also liked the slide. They learned to be careful in the fog. They learned that sometimes things go wrong, but mom is always there to help.
